If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% in early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1–2% in mid horizon (8–15 days) to compensate for bearish bias.  
If sentiment swings from positive to negative within 5 days, shift forecast downward by 1–3% in late horizon (16–30 days) to reflect sentiment reversal.  
When sentiment is consistently neutral (0.00–0.33) over 7 days, apply a 0.5–1.5% downward bias across all horizons to avoid flat forecast drift.  
If sentiment peaks >0.80 in last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1–3% in early horizon to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is negative and forecast is rising, reverse direction by 0.5–1.5% in mid horizon to align with sentiment-driven correction.
